body:
Dev Patel: Heads up — early inbound from the new lifecycle emails + console banners. Nothing on fire, but a few recurring “confused” notes. Flagging here so we can tweak copy fast before we scale volume. :eyes:

Dev Patel: Themes from ~12 convos since yesterday:
1) Email CTA confusion: “Go to Console to create an API key” → folks land on dashboard and don’t see “API keys” right away.
2) Console banner wording: “Enable streaming for lower latency” is getting challenged (“streaming doesn’t change latency?”).
3) People don’t know what “Route” means (“Do I need Dedicated? Is a route a deployment?”).
4) A couple users thought the checklist was required before *any* request.

Aparna Reddy: +1. On my end, 2 users asked if they need billing to test (“I don’t want to add a card just to see if it works”). They’re reading “production-like” and assuming paywall.

Support Bot: Jira created/linked: SUP-2841 “Onboarding email link lands on wrong console path / 404” (reporter: Support)

Dev Patel: ^ also seeing that. One user screenshot shows a 404 after clicking “Create API key” from Email #1.

Tyler Benson: Thanks for pulling this together. Can you paste the exact link you saw in the email? Might be a routing change + stale path in the template.

Dev Patel: Here’s the one from the ticket:
`https://console.redwoodinference.com/projects/new/api-keys?utm_source=...`
User says it redirects to `/projects` then 404s.

Marissa Cole: That path is old; we moved keys under project settings in the last console nav update. We should update CTAs to:
`/console/projects/{project_id}/settings/api-keys`
(or the generic “Create a project” flow if they don’t have one yet).

Ben Carter: Copy tweaks we can do today:
- Email CTA: instead of “Create an API key” → “Open Console → Settings → API Keys”
- Add 1-line “Don’t have a project yet? Create one first (takes ~30s).”
Tyler can you swap links?

Tyler Benson: Yep. I’ll update template links + UTMs. Need the preferred canonical path (Marissa) + any tracking constraints.

Paula Mendes: For tracking: please keep UTMs intact, but avoid adding extra query params beyond our convention. Also please don’t include user identifiers.

Soojin Lee: Re banner copy: we should not claim “lower latency” for streaming. It’s lower *time-to-first-token* / better perceived responsiveness. Suggest:
“Turn on streaming to get the first token faster and improve UX.”
And add a tooltip “Total completion time depends on output length + model.”

Kenji Nakamura: +1. The current banner is too absolute. Also “Enable streaming” sounds like a settings hunt. We can say “Try streaming responses” and link to a code snippet modal.

Dev Patel: Here are 3 user quotes (verbatim-ish):
- “I turned on streaming and it’s still slow.”
- “What’s a route? Am I deploying something?”
- “Do I have to finish all checklist steps before the API works?”

Jada Williams: For checklist: we can change the header text from “Complete setup” to “Recommended next steps” and add an (optional) label on items.

Leila Farouk: Also saw one user click the banner twice because it didn’t look dismissible. If we tweak copy, can we also add “Dismiss” affordance? (or at least make the X more obvious)

Marissa Cole: Dismiss is already there but subtle. We can tweak styling in the next patch, but copy changes are quickest.

Logan Wright: Re “Route” language: that’s also showing up in events + dashboards. If we rename in UI, please loop me in so taxonomy doesn’t drift. But for copy, we can define it.

Ben Carter: Maybe simplest: avoid “Route” in emails entirely.
Use “Create a deployment endpoint” / “Create an inference endpoint” and only introduce “route” once they’re in console.

Soojin Lee: Agree. “Route” is internal-ish. For devs, “endpoint” is clearer.
Suggested replacements:
- Email: “Create your first endpoint (hosted)”
- Console checklist item: “Create a route (endpoint)” with helper text.

Tyler Benson: Action items I’m hearing:
1) Fix email link destinations (SUP-2841) + update CTA label.
2) Remove “lower latency” claim → “faster first token” in banner.
3) Replace “route” with “endpoint” in emails; add inline definition in console.

Dev Patel: Yes. Also please add a line in Email #2 (or troubleshooting email) that you can run a first request without billing. That question is eating cycles.

Ben Carter: Good call. We can add:
“No credit card required to make your first request. Add billing when you’re ready to scale.”
(Soojin: ok with that?)

Soojin Lee: Yes, as long as it’s accurate for all regions/segments. If any geo requires billing upfront, we need a qualifier. But I *think* we’re good.

Marissa Cole: It’s accurate today. Billing is required for higher limits, not first success.

Paula Mendes: Please keep “no card required” phrasing consistent across channels; we’ve had confusion when ads say one thing and console says another.

Dev Patel: I’ll update our support macros too once copy lands.

Tyler Benson: ETA: link fixes + email copy tweak can ship today if I get final strings by 3pm PT.

Ben Carter: I’ll draft updates in the copy doc and tag @Soojin Lee + @Dev Patel for quick review.

Kenji Nakamura: I’ll propose revised banner text + helper tooltip string in the nudge copy deck and ping @Marissa Cole to confirm it fits the component.

Dev Patel: Thanks all. Please keep me in the loop when it goes live — we’ll watch ticket volume and share any new edge cases here. :thumbsup:
